title: At someone's home
goal: Visit a friend's family, be a good guest (and host), accept and turn down food the way people really do, help out, stay the night, and talk about what you used to do.
intro:
Sooner or later a friend will say **کبھی چکر لگاؤ نا!** — 'drop by sometime!' — and mean it. A visit to a Pakistani home has its own script: a loud welcome, greeting the parents as **آنٹی** and **انکل**, food you can't really refuse, an offer to help that will be waved away, and long **گپ شپ** that easily turns into staying the night.

This unit gives you that script. You'll learn the **habitual past** for 'used to' (**ہم اکٹھے اسکول جاتے تھے** 'we used to go to school together'), how friends and families **offer and decline** (with the coaxing particle **نا**), and how to say 'shall I…?' and 'is it OK if I…?' with **دوں** and **لوں**. Notice the switch: **تم** with your friend, **آپ** with their parents.

grammar.title: "Used to": the habitual past کرتا تھا
grammar.body:
To talk about what used to happen — childhood, old routines, 'back in the hostel' — Urdu uses the **habitual past**. It is the -تا / -تی / -تے form you know from the present habitual (unit 10), with **تھا / تھی / تھے / تھیں** in place of ہوں / ہے / ہیں:

میں جاتا **تھا** (man) · میں جاتی **تھی** (woman)
تم جاتے **تھے** · تم جاتی **تھیں**
وہ جاتا **تھا** / جاتی **تھی** · ہم، آپ، وہ (pl.) جاتے **تھے**
women and respected women: جاتی **تھیں**

It translates English 'used to', 'would' (for habits) and often a simple past with 'always', 'every…': بچپن میں ہم ہر گرمیوں میں یہاں **آتے تھے** 'as kids we came here every summer'.

**No نے:** unlike the simple past, the habitual past never takes نے, even with transitive verbs, and the verb agrees with the subject: ہم گپ شپ **کرتے تھے** (not ہم نے).

**The trap:** don't mix it up with the simple past. ہم یہاں **آئے** = we came (once); ہم یہاں **آتے تھے** = we used to come. And the dative 'feelings' verbs work the same way: مجھے نیند نہیں **آتی تھی** 'I used to have trouble sleeping'.

Useful time words: **پہلے** 'before, in the past', **بچپن میں** 'as a child', **اُس زمانے میں** 'back then', **ہر…** 'every…'. To bring up a shared memory, start with **یاد ہے، …؟** 'remember how…?'.

grammar.title: Offering and declining like a local
grammar.body:
In unit 18 you met formal hospitality (تشریف رکھیے، تکلف نہ کریں). Among friends and their families it is warmer, louder and more insistent.

**Offering:** the standard offer is a **future question**: **چائے پیو گے؟** 'will you have tea?' (to a male friend), **کچھ کھاؤ گی؟** (to a female friend), polite **کیا لیں گے؟**. Pushing more food on you: **اور لو نا!**, **تھوڑا سا اور**, **شرمانا نہیں** 'don't be shy'.

**The particle نا:** said after a request, **نا** makes it coaxing — 'go on!', 'come on!': **لو نا**, **بیٹھو نا**, **کبھی چکر لگاؤ نا**. After a statement it asks for agreement: رک رہی ہو **نا**؟ 'you're staying, aren't you?'. Don't confuse it with **نہ** 'not', which comes *before* the verb.

**Declining:** the first 'no' is not taken seriously, so give a reason: **بس، پیٹ بھر گیا** 'that's it, I'm full', **ابھی کھا کر آیا ہوں** 'I've just eaten', with a hand on your chest or over your plate. To give in gracefully: **اچھا، تھوڑا سا** 'OK, just a little'.

**Register:** with your friend use تم forms (لو، بیٹھو، آؤ); with their parents switch to **آپ** (لیں، بیٹھیں) and call them **آنٹی / انکل**. Aunty will call you **بیٹا** or **بیٹی** and use تم — that's affection, not rudeness.

examples.en: Tea or a cold drink? (to a male friend)
Oh, go on, have some more!

grammar.title: Shall I…? Is it OK if I…? دوں and لوں
grammar.body:
As a guest you constantly ask 'shall I…?' and 'is it OK if I…?'. Both use the **subjunctive** (unit 18) of a helper verb after the stem:

**stem + دوں؟** — 'shall I (do it for you)?', an offer to help: **برتن دھو دوں؟** 'shall I do the dishes?', **لائٹ بند کر دوں؟** 'shall I switch the light off?'

**stem + لوں؟** — 'is it OK if I (do it for myself)?', asking permission: **واش روم استعمال کر لوں؟** 'can I use the bathroom?', **تھوڑی دیر لیٹ جاؤں؟** 'can I lie down for a bit?'

The subjunctive does not change for gender, so men and women say the same. Add **کیا** at the front to sound a little more formal; among friends the question intonation is enough.

For house rules, use the 'have to' pattern from unit 15: **جوتے اتارنے ہیں؟** 'do I need to take my shoes off?', and the plain subjunctive for 'where/what shall I…': **سامان کہاں رکھوں؟** 'where shall I put my things?'.

**Replies:** the host's standard answer to any offer of help is **ارے نہیں، رہنے دو** 'oh no, leave it'. Insist once with **نہیں، مجھے کرنے دو** 'no, let me do it'.

culture: Visiting is the backbone of social life in Pakistan, and close friends and relatives rarely need an appointment: they just **چکر لگاتے ہیں**, especially in the evening and at weekends. Bring something — a box of sweets from a well-known local shop, fruit, or for close friends something hot from the bazaar — and never arrive خالی ہاتھ. Greet the parents first: **السلام علیکم آنٹی / انکل**, with آپ; uncles often hug young men, and aunties may pat a girl on the head. Food will keep coming, and the polite refuse–insist–accept routine is expected, so if you really can't eat more, refuse twice and cover your plate. Many homes keep shoes on in the drawing room but take them off in bedrooms or where people pray — when unsure, ask **جوتے اتار دوں؟**. Offering to help in the kitchen is appreciated even though you'll be told **رہنے دو**; at a close friend's, quietly clearing your own plate wins you points. Staying over is common among close friends (for young women, usually after the parents have spoken). In the diaspora the same rules hold — plus one more: you will not be allowed to leave without a container of leftovers.

tip.title: Your friend is تم, their parents are آپ
tip.body:
- With your friend: **تم** and **یار** — آؤ، بیٹھو، کب آئے؟
- With their parents: **آپ**, plural verbs, and **آنٹی / انکل**: آنٹی، آپ کیسی **ہیں**؟
- Aunty will call you **بیٹا / بیٹی** and use تم: that's affection, not rudeness.

tip.title: Offers, نا, and saying no twice
tip.body:
- Friends offer with a **future question**: چائے پیو **گے**؟ (to a man), کچھ کھاؤ **گی**؟ (to a woman).
- **نا** after a request coaxes — 'go on!': اور لو **نا**!
- The first 'no' doesn't count: give a reason — **بس، پیٹ بھر گیا** — and give in with **اچھا، تھوڑا سا**.

lessons.title: When we were kids…

tip.title: Used to: جاتا تھا
tip.body:
- 'Used to' = the habitual **-تا / -تی / -تے** + **تھا / تھی / تھے**: ہم اکٹھے اسکول **جاتے تھے**.
- **No نے**, even with transitive verbs: ہم کرکٹ **کھیلتے تھے**.
- Don't mix it with the simple past: ہم یہاں **آئے** 'we came (once)' vs ہم یہاں **آتے تھے** 'we used to come'.

sentences.en: As kids we used to go to Nani's every Eid.

sentences.native: ہم دونوں ایک ہی اسکول میں پڑھتے تھے۔
sentences.roman: ham donoṃ ek hī iskūl meṃ paṛhte the.
sentences.en: We both used to go to the same school.

sentences.native: ہم اکٹھے کرکٹ کھیلتے تھے۔
sentences.roman: ham ikaṭṭhe krikeṭ khelte the.
sentences.en: We used to play cricket together.

sentences.native: ابو ہر اتوار کو ناشتہ بناتے تھے۔
sentences.roman: abbū har itvār ko nāshta banāte the.
sentences.en: Dad used to make breakfast every Sunday.

sentences.native: پہلے مجھے رات کو نیند نہیں آتی تھی۔
sentences.roman: pahle mujhe rāt ko nīnd nahīṃ ātī thī.
sentences.en: I used to have trouble sleeping at night.

sentences.native: کیا تم پہلے بھی یہاں رہتے تھے؟
sentences.roman: kyā tum pahle bhī yahāṃ rahte the?
sentences.en: Did you use to live here before as well?

sentences.native: نانی کے گھر بہت اچھی نیند آتی تھی۔
sentences.roman: nānī ke ghar bahut achchhī nīnd ātī thī.
sentences.en: I always slept so well at Nani's.

sentences.native: تمہیں دیر سے اٹھنے کی عادت تھی۔
sentences.roman: tumheṃ der se uṭhne kī ʿādat thī.
sentences.en: You always used to get up late. (lit. had the habit of)

sentences.native: مجھے صبح کی چائے کی عادت ہے۔
sentences.roman: mujhe subah kī chā’e kī ʿādat hai.
sentences.en: I can't do without my morning tea. (lit. I have the habit)

sentences.native: ہم پہلے روز ملتے تھے، اب مہینوں نہیں ملتے۔
sentences.roman: ham pahle roz milte the, ab mahīnoṃ nahīṃ milte.
sentences.en: We used to meet every day; now we go months without meeting.

tip.title: Shall I…? stem + دوں
tip.body:
- Offer to help with **stem + دوں؟** 'shall I (do it for you)?': برتن دھو **دوں**؟، میز سمیٹ **دوں**؟
- It's the same for men and women.
- Expect **ارے نہیں، رہنے دو** 'oh no, leave it' — insist once: **نہیں، مجھے کرنے دو**.

sentences.native: میں بھی ہاتھ بٹا دوں؟
sentences.roman: maiṃ bhī hāth baṭā dūṃ?
sentences.en: Shall I give you a hand too?

sentences.native: میں میز سمیٹ دوں؟
sentences.roman: maiṃ mez sameṭ dūṃ?
sentences.en: Shall I clear the table?

sentences.native: آنٹی، میں چائے بنا دوں؟
sentences.roman: ānṭī, maiṃ chā’e banā dūṃ?
sentences.en: Aunty, shall I make the tea?

sentences.native: جھاڑو کہاں ہے؟ میں لگا دیتی ہوں۔
sentences.roman: jhāṛū kahāṃ hai? maiṃ lagā detī hūṃ.
sentences.en: Where's the broom? I'll sweep. (woman)

sentences.native: آج ماسی نہیں آئی، سب کو صفائی کرنی ہے۔
sentences.roman: āj māsī nahīṃ ā’ī, sab ko safā’ī karnī hai.
sentences.en: The maid hasn't come today, so everyone has to clean.

sentences.native: ارے نہیں، رہنے دو، ماسی کل کر دے گی۔
sentences.roman: are nahīṃ, rahne do, māsī kal kar de gī.
sentences.en: Oh no, leave it, the maid will do it tomorrow.

sentences.native: آج برتن دھونے کی تمہاری باری ہے۔
sentences.roman: āj bartan dhone kī tumhārī bārī hai.
sentences.en: It's your turn to do the dishes today.

sentences.native: کمرہ سمیٹ لو، آنٹی آ رہی ہیں!
sentences.roman: kamra sameṭ lo, ānṭī ā rahī haiṃ!
sentences.en: Tidy up the room, Aunty's coming!

sentences.native: تم مہمان ہو، تم کچھ نہیں کرو گے۔
sentences.roman: tum mehmān ho, tum kuchh nahīṃ karo ge.
sentences.en: You're a guest — you're not doing a thing.

sentences.native: گھر میں سب صفائی میں ہاتھ بٹاتے ہیں۔
sentences.roman: ghar meṃ sab safā’ī meṃ hāth baṭāte haiṃ.
sentences.en: Everyone at home helps with the cleaning.

lessons.title: House rules and asking first

tip.title: Is it OK if I…? stem + لوں
tip.body:
- Ask permission with **stem + لوں؟** 'is it OK if I (do it for myself)?': واش روم استعمال کر **لوں**؟
- Compare: کر **دوں**؟ = shall I do it *for you*? · کر **لوں**؟ = may I do it *for me*?
- House rules use 'have to': جوتے **اتارنے ہیں**؟

new: وائی فائی کا پاس ورڈ کیا ہے؟

sentences.native: میں ذرا واش روم استعمال کر لوں؟
sentences.roman: maiṃ zarā vāsh rūm istiʿmāl kar lūṃ?
sentences.en: Is it OK if I just use the bathroom?

sentences.native: میں تمہارا فون استعمال کر لوں؟ میرا بند ہو گیا۔
sentences.roman: maiṃ tumhārā fon istiʿmāl kar lūṃ? merā band ho gayā.
sentences.en: Can I use your phone? Mine's died.

sentences.native: میں تھوڑی دیر آرام کر لوں؟
sentences.roman: maiṃ thoṛī der ārām kar lūṃ?
sentences.en: Is it OK if I rest for a bit?

sentences.native: میں تھوڑی دیر لیٹ جاؤں؟
sentences.roman: maiṃ thoṛī der leṭ jā’ūṃ?
sentences.en: Is it OK if I lie down for a bit?

sentences.native: کیا جوتے اتارنے ہیں؟
sentences.roman: kyā jūte utārne haiṃ?
sentences.en: Do I need to take my shoes off?

sentences.native: اپنے کپڑے کہاں رکھوں؟
sentences.roman: apne kapṛe kahāṃ rakhūṃ?
sentences.en: Where shall I put my clothes?

sentences.native: جوتے یہاں اتار لو۔
sentences.roman: jūte yahāṃ utār lo.
sentences.en: Take your shoes off here. (informal)

sentences.native: گیزر چلا دو، پانی بہت ٹھنڈا ہے۔
sentences.roman: gīzar chalā do, pānī bahut ṭhanḍā hai.
sentences.en: Turn the water heater on, the water's freezing.

sentences.native: وائی فائی نہیں چل رہا، پاس ورڈ بدل گیا ہے؟
sentences.roman: vā’ī fā’ī nahīṃ chal rahā, pās varḍ badal gayā hai?
sentences.en: The wifi isn't working — has the password changed?

sentences.native: ایک اور تکیہ مل جائے گا؟
sentences.roman: ek aur takiya mil jā’e gā?
sentences.en: Could I have another pillow?

sentences.native: رات کو سردی ہوگی، کمبل لے لو۔
sentences.roman: rāt ko sardī hogī, kambal le lo.
sentences.en: It'll be cold tonight — take a blanket.

sentences.native: امی نے تمہارے لیے نئی چادر لگا دی ہے۔
sentences.roman: ammī ne tumhāre liye na’ī chādar lagā dī hai.
sentences.en: Mum has put a fresh sheet on for you.

sentences.native: لائٹ پھر چلی گئی، گیزر بھی بند ہے۔
sentences.roman: lā’iṭ phir chalī ga’ī, gīzar bhī band hai.
sentences.en: The power's gone again, and the water heater's off too.

sentences.native: بچپن میں لائٹ جاتی تھی تو ہم چھت پر سوتے تھے۔
sentences.roman: bachpan meṃ lā’iṭ jātī thī to ham chhat par sote the.
sentences.en: When we were kids, whenever the power went we'd sleep on the roof.

sentences.native: رک جاؤ نا، صبح ناشتہ کر کے جانا۔
sentences.roman: ruk jā’o nā, subah nāshta kar ke jānā.
sentences.en: Do stay — you can leave after breakfast.

sentences.native: مجھے یہاں بہت اچھی نیند آئی۔
sentences.roman: mujhe yahāṃ bahut achchhī nīnd ā’ī.
sentences.en: I slept really well here.

sentences.native: ابھی رکو، کھانا کھا کر جانا!
sentences.roman: abhī ruko, khānā khā kar jānā!
sentences.en: Stay a bit — have dinner before you go!

sentences.native: اب مجھے جانا چاہیے، کافی دیر ہو گئی۔
sentences.roman: ab mujhe jānā chāhiye, kāfī der ho ga’ī.
sentences.en: I should head off now, it's got quite late.
